# Record 88 credits a mechanism that did not run, and the correction is worth more than the sentence

The seventh review passed the ticket and left one low finding, which is this. Record 88 says its cross-attempt
citation of records 76 and 77 was carried by the commit search tolerating the ticket file. At the tree that
record was written against, nothing counted had moved at all: commit `1a7f8e7` reverted the ticket file by exactly
the inverse of `82e181b`, plus eight and minus seventy-five against plus seventy-five and minus eight, so its
content fingerprint is `804bab59a5d4`, which is green 77's own tree. Replaying `cited_check` with those records
returns at the identity branch. No commit search ran, no substitution, no scoped comparison.

So the record describes a more generous mechanism than the one that granted it. A later session, or the
calibration asking which record first carried evidence through the procedure-rewrite tolerance, would point at
record 88 and find the identity branch instead.

**It cuts the safe way, which is worth saying plainly rather than as a defence.** The gate accepted on the
strongest ground available, an exactly equal tree, and not on a weaker one. And the claim becomes true of what is
being delivered: once the Outcome moved the ticket file again, the tolerant path does run, and the reviewer
replayed the same pair accepted through it at the delivered tree. Record 88 is accepted and the journal is
append-only, so this note is the correction rather than an edit, and the Outcome now says which branch ran when.

**The counterfactual that mattered came back a clear yes, and the reviewer did not take it from the code.**
Replaying the same citation shape with attempt 6's pair, whose slice files did move, is refused by name: "The code
check 66 covers has changed since it ran: harness/gates.py, harness/tests/test_stage_gates.py", and `_moved_since`
bites on each of `harness/gates.py`, `harness/handoff.py`, `harness/tests/test_stage_gates.py` and
`harness/tests/test_session_cap.py` individually. Had any of the four moved, this citation would have been refused
the same way. The rule did not accept its own author's evidence on a weaker test than it applies to anyone else,
which was the thing to be suspicious of and the reason it was put to the review as a blocking question.

The other four corrections were checked against the artefacts rather than the prose and hold: no refusal kind
exists in any journal in this repository and a harness refusal raises without writing, so "no stage refusal is
recorded anywhere" is the right form of the claim; record 76's stored output contains no `ValueError` at all;
`c11c903` carries the return with 231 inserted lines of `gates.py` and four other files while `34f2511` carries
six journal records and nothing else; and the pair rule does run in a second loop after the slice loop, so the
attribution is what a session sees.
